archetypes.name: test-env-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan mutates four eval-isolation test sites and adds one new integration test; any missed export or inner bash-c export list omission silently breaks under set -u.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan adds DEDUP_PLAN_LINES_PY as a new env var that must be exported in four separate eval-isolation test sites and in each site's inner bash -c export list; verify the plan explicitly covers all four sites and does not assume a single top-of-script assignment propagates into awk-extracted eval contexts. Check whether the new integration test's PYWRAP correctly captures REAL_PYTHON before mutating PATH, and whether the basename matching logic is specific enough to intercept only dedup-plan-lines.py without touching the findings-dedup helper .plan-review-loop-dedup.py. Confirm the non-numeric stub is changed from any stdin-reading heredoc-era shape to a deterministic bogus-output form, as required by the Edge Cases section. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sibling-doc-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan creates a new .md sibling contract doc whose invariant wording must not contradict the Python logic, especially around fenced duplicate-collapse behavior versus heading/Constraints-state suppression.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan creates dedup-plan-lines.md as the authoritative contract for the new helper and requires a one-line addition to parse-plan-commands.md; verify the stated invariants (CLI shape, fence model, Constraints protection scope, duplicate-collapse behavior inside fences) are internally self-consistent and do not conflict with how the Python logic is described elsewhere in the plan. Check whether the cross-reference wording in parse-plan-commands.md correctly scopes the divergence to heading and Constraints-state detection without implying that fenced regions protect duplicate lines from collapse, since the plan's Edge Cases section explicitly warns against that claim. Confirm the module docstring planned for dedup-plan-lines.py accurately reflects the two-pass balanced-pair semantics and the failed-closer behavior, and that neither doc overstates the Constraints protection as applying inside fences. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: exclusion-scope-audit
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds two agent-lint.toml exclusions via variableized-caller reasoning; misplaced or under-commented entries can silently weaken dead-script or sibling-doc lint globally.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan adds dedup-plan-lines.py to the dead-script exclusion block and dedup-plan-lines.md to the sibling-md exclusion block in agent-lint.toml; verify the plan's proposed block placement and comment format match the existing conventions in that file, and that the caller comment naming plan-review-loop.sh and $DEDUP_PLAN_LINES_PY is specific enough for a future maintainer to locate and remove the exclusion if the caller changes. Check whether the plan's instruction to add the entries unconditionally (rather than conditionally on some lint version) is consistent with how other variableized-caller exclusions are handled in agent-lint.toml today. Confirm the plan does not place the new entries in a broad catch-all block that would weaken global dead-script or sibling-doc coverage beyond the two specific new files. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
